text:
Sara: Hey team — I addressed the two blocking nits on PR #4321 and force-pushed. Main change: switch canary merge ordering so migrations run after traffic shift. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/4321
Dmitri: Nice, thanks. Can you paste the e2e failure you were hitting before? I want to make sure the ordering won't race with the shard allocator.
Sara: The failing trace was the kv-allocator asserting on empty-assignment. Repro steps were flaky under parallel canary. I added a tiny sleep in migration job and a guard: ```python
if not assignments:
    return
``` which fixed the race in my local runs.
ci-bot: CI job #4321.3 — tests: passed (unit: 145, integration: 12) — artifacts: https://ci.example/4321/3 :white_check_mark:
Jen: PTAL please — I have one more approval and we can merge into canary today at 15:00 PST. Also check the migration guard is safe for on-prem (no silent skips).
Alejandro: Quick note — can we avoid sleeping for >50ms? That can add up on large rollouts. Maybe use an exponential backoff or check assignment version instead.
Sara: Good call. Swapped the sleep for a version-check loop (10ms max) — snippet: ```diff
- time.sleep(0.05)
+ for _ in range(5):
+    if assignments.version == expected_version:
+        break
+    time.sleep(0.01)
```
Dmitri: Code lgtm, left one tiny nit about logging level. Otherwise :+1:
Sara: Fixed logging level to DEBUG -> INFO and pushed. Thanks!
Jen: I'll grab the second approval in 30m and merge after the canary window opens. If anyone objects, speak now.
Alejandro: No objections from my side.
Sara: Merged and queued canary rollout at 15:05 PST. Thanks everyone :tada:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for PR #4321 — batch=1/10 — rolling back automatically on 5% error rate. Monitor: https://console.redwood.example/rollouts/4321
